notes.meaning: An honest person living in poverty is far better off than a wealthy fool who speaks deceitfully. Upright character and a clear conscience are worth much more than riches or social status.

Having strong enthusiasm does no good if a person lacks true knowledge and understanding. Rushing ahead without thinking things through causes people to stumble, miss the path of duty, and fall into sin.

People often ruin their own lives through foolish choices and rebellious behavior. Instead of admitting their own fault, their hearts grow angry and blame God for the trouble they brought on themselves.
Money easily attracts crowds of companions who stay close only for what they can get. When someone loses their wealth, those shallow friends walk away and leave them all alone.
Anyone who lies in court or spreads falsehoods in daily life will face punishment. Even if human judges fail to catch them, God sees the truth and will make sure liars answer for their wickedness.
Many people flatter leaders and seek the favor of rulers who have power and honor to give out. Almost everyone wants to be the friend of someone who distributes gifts freely.
When someone falls into deep poverty, even their own relatives often treat them coldly and stay away. The poor person may plead for help, but former friends disappear when they are needed most.
A person who works hard to gain wisdom and godly understanding is showing true love to their own soul. Guarding that understanding and living by it brings lasting good and true success.
God repeats the warning against lying because dishonest words cause so much destruction. A person who continually tells lies will not escape judgment, but will bring about their own final ruin.

Living in luxury and delicate ease does not suit a fool, who will only use prosperity to do more harm. It is even more unfitting when an unruly servant is put in charge of leaders and treats others with cruel arrogance.
Good sense helps a person stay calm and keep from exploding in anger. Real honor comes not from demanding revenge, but from choosing to forgive and overlook an insult.
The anger of a king is terrifying, like the roar of a hungry lion ready to strike. In contrast, the ruler's goodwill brings relief and life, like morning dew reviving grass in dry weather.
A rebellious and foolish son brings heartbreak and ruin to his father. An argumentative, nagging wife is like a leaky roof that drips water constantly and makes the whole house miserable.
Houses and wealth can be passed down from earthly parents through family inheritance. A wise, sensible, and gentle wife, however, is a special blessing that comes straight from the Lord's care.
Laziness numbs a person's mind and makes them useless, as if they were trapped in a deep sleep. Anyone who refuses to do honest work will eventually run out of food and go hungry.
Obeying God's commandments guards a person's life and brings true spiritual peace. But anyone who lives carelessly and pays no attention to God's standards is walking toward death and destruction.
Showing mercy to the poor is treated by God as making a loan directly to Him. The Lord takes personal note of every kind deed done for the needy and will generously repay the giver.

Parents must correct their children early, while their hearts can still be shaped and there is hope for change. Refusing to discipline a child out of weak pity leaves them to continue in evil, which leads to their destruction.

A hot-tempered person continually lands in trouble and must pay the price for wild outbursts. If you step in and bail them out, their uncontrolled anger will quickly create another mess that requires saving them all over again.
Wisdom begins by humbly listening to good advice and accepting correction when you are wrong. Those who submit to instruction in their youth will reap the reward of wisdom later in life.
Human beings come up with many schemes and plans in their own minds. In the end, God's unchanging purpose is the only one that stands firm and accomplishes what He desires.

What makes a person truly valued is a loyal, kind heart that genuinely wants to do good. A poor person who has goodwill but lacks money is far better than a rich person who makes empty promises and lies.

Living with deep reverence and respect toward the Lord leads to a full and satisfying life. A person who walks with God finds restful peace and is kept from the spiritual ruin that overtakes the wicked.

This humorous picture shows how ridiculous extreme laziness can become. The sluggard is so lazy that after reaching his hand into the food bowl, he will not even make the effort to lift the food back to his mouth.

Punishing a hardened scorner teaches inexperienced people to take warning and stay away from evil. On the other hand, a wise person does not need physical blows; a gentle verbal rebuke is enough to teach him more knowledge.

A son who mistreats his parents by wasting his father's hard-earned money or driving his mother out of the home is wicked and unnatural. Such shameful cruelty ruins his own name and brings disgrace on the whole family.

Staying on the right path requires paying continuous attention to truth. The moment a person stops listening to sound instruction, they begin to drift away from the words of knowledge and fall into error.
A dishonest witness sneers at justice and treats the duty of speaking the truth as a joke. Wicked people take such delight in wrongdoing that they swallow sin down greedily like a tasty meal.
Those who mock serious, holy things cannot escape their coming punishment. God has sure penalties prepared for scorners, and severe discipline is waiting for the backs of fools.
